discovery: Spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots: proposal and experimental realization of coherent control and readout of single electron spins

nominees.name: Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
nominees.affiliation: QuTech and Delft University of Technology, Netherlands

subfield: Condensed matter physics / mesoscopic physics and quantum information
motivation: In 1998 Loss (with DiVincenzo) proposed using the spin of a single electron confined in a gate-defined semiconductor quantum dot as a qubit, with exchange coupling between neighbouring dots providing two-qubit gates. This turned Coulomb-blockade physics of mesoscopic transport into a blueprint for quantum computing. Experiment followed: Marcus and co-workers demonstrated coherent singlet-triplet control and spin echo in double dots, revealing and overcoming hyperfine decoherence, while Vandersypen and co-workers achieved single-shot spin readout, electrically driven single-spin rotations and, later, high-fidelity two-qubit gates and multi-qubit processors in silicon. Together these works established the electron spin in a nanostructure as a controllable quantum object, combining deep theory of decoherence and noise with remarkable device engineering. The field now underpins industrial efforts toward CMOS-compatible quantum processors, a direct path from fundamental mesoscopic physics to quantum technology.
